description: Essential cooking methods, techniques, and culinary knowledge

dry_heat.roasting: Uncovered in oven; high heat; develops crust via Maillard reaction
dry_heat.baking: Covered or uncovered oven; lower, consistent heat
dry_heat.grilling: Direct heat from below; char marks, smoky flavor
dry_heat.broiling: Direct heat from above; similar to grilling
dry_heat.sautéing: Small amount of fat in hot pan; quick cooking with constant motion
dry_heat.stir_frying: High heat in wok; constant motion; Asian technique
dry_heat.pan_frying: More fat than sautéing; submerged on one side
dry_heat.deep_frying: Fully submerged in hot oil; crunchy exterior

moist_heat.steaming: Above boiling water; retains nutrients; vegetables, fish, dim sum
moist_heat.braising: Brown then slow-cook in liquid; tough cuts become tender
moist_heat.stewing: Fully submerged in liquid; long slow cooking

combination.pressure_cooking: Steam pressure raises boiling point; fast cooking
combination.sous_vide: Vacuum-sealed bag in precise temperature water bath; precise results

knife_skills.grip: Pinch grip on blade near bolster for control

cuts.mirepoix: 1–2cm rough dice; for stocks and soups
cuts.chiffonade: Thin ribbons of leafy herbs or greens

knife_skills.maintenance: Hone blade before each use; sharpen every few months

flavor_building.maillard_reaction: Browning reaction between amino acids and sugars at ~140°C+; creates complex flavors
flavor_building.caramelization: Sugar breakdown at 160°C+; sweet, nutty flavors
flavor_building.umami: Fifth taste; from glutamates; found in aged cheese, mushrooms, soy, tomatoes
flavor_building.seasoning: Salt enhances flavor; acid balances richness; fat carries flavor
flavor_building.blooming_spices: Toast in dry pan or hot oil to release essential oils

mother_sauces.béchamel: Roux + milk; base for cheese sauces
mother_sauces.velouté: Roux + white stock; base for cream sauces
mother_sauces.espagnole: Brown roux + brown stock; rich meat sauces
mother_sauces.hollandaise: Emulsified egg yolk + butter; béarnaise is derivative

sauces_classical.emulsification: Stable mixture of two unmixable liquids (oil and water) via emulsifier (egg yolk, mustard)

baking_science.gluten: Protein formed when flour proteins (glutenin, gliadin) hydrate; provides structure

leavening.yeast: Biological; produces CO₂ and alcohol via fermentation
leavening.baking_soda: Chemical; reacts with acid to produce CO₂
leavening.baking_powder: Chemical; contains acid and base; reacts with moisture and heat

baking_science.fat_role: Shortens gluten strands (tenderness), adds richness, carries flavor

food_safety.fifo: First In, First Out; use oldest ingredients first
food_safety.cross_contamination: Keep raw meat separate from ready-to-eat foods
